note: The curriculum's figures (Ceetrix story 7). Each is drawn by figures/make_figures.py into figures/<id>.svg, and printed from figures/print/<id>.svg in its print state. coach says where the coach shows it (a story, or a lesson step); book names the Markdown file and the sentence its marker follows. validate.py checks every word, the placement, the states and the arithmetic.

figures.title: Where the words go
figures.alt: Priya's laptop and printer inside her network. Last year an arrow leaves her network for a company's computers far away. On Tuesday the arrow goes to backroom, the box on the shelf, inside her network.
figures.caption: Same app, same letter. What changed is where it goes.

book.after: A box on a shelf, talking to a laptop on a desk, above a bakery.

figures.title: Spot the line
figures.alt: A sample list of where each program is sending data. Line 1: the chat app to backroom. Line 2: the printer app to the printer. Line 3: the chat app to a company's computers far away, the line that shouldn't be there.
figures.caption: A made-up bad Wednesday. Nothing beeps; the list is how you find out.

book.after: It's an open window in a house you've just locked up: the house doesn't tell you, you go and look.

figures.title: Three stations, three amounts of you
figures.alt: Three stations on one line: What can my computer do?, an amber diamond; Local chat, a grey circle; Is my chat app talking to anyone else?, a red triangle with an exclamation mark.
figures.caption: Priya's three stations. The shape says the same as the colour, so it reads in black and white too.

options.label: Is my chat app talking to anyone else?

figures.title: The room and the warehouse
figures.alt: A 2 TB drive drawn as a long warehouse, and 16 GB of memory drawn as a room with a half mark. A model file sits in the warehouse, or is loaded into the room, where a 20 GB file spills out.
figures.caption: A 16 GB laptop with a 2 TB drive. The file can sit in the warehouse all day; it only runs in the room.

book.after: The choir doesn't sing in the warehouse. 😆

figures.title: Will it fit?
figures.alt: Your memory drawn as a room with a half mark, and a model file drawn to the same scale inside it, spilling out past the end when it is bigger than the room.
figures.caption: Pick your memory, then a file. Under half fits; bigger than the room doesn't; in between, it depends.

book.after: (I haven't measured this rule on an 8 GB machine, where your computer's own share of the room is bigger. If yours says 8, treat "fits" as "depends" until I have.)

figures.title: One file, nothing to call
figures.alt: One 5 GB model file, copied to another machine. On a machine with enough memory it fits; on a 4 GB laptop it doesn't run. No line goes anywhere else.
figures.caption: The whole model is the file. Copy it to another machine, and it runs there too if the room is big enough.

book.after: The model needs more than its file, too. The **model file** is the one file you download (the whole of the clever part in one lump, closer to a film file than to an app). Running it also takes **working space**: the program that runs it, the conversation so far, and a few helpers I'll name in Book 2.
